title: The bomb steered by pigeons
caption:
In WW2, an American guided bomb was designed to be flown by pigeons. Seriously. 🐦
A trained pigeon pecked at the target's image on a screen in the nose: when the target drifted off centre, its pecks steered the bomb back. Three birds, so two could outvote one.
Would you trust a pigeon over 1940s electronics? Yes or no?
first_comment: Three pigeons and a majority vote is more democracy than most group chats 🗳️🐦
sources: Smithsonian Magazine, 'B.F. Skinner's Pigeon-Guided Rocket' (2011): pigeons trained to peck at a target image on a screen in the nose cone to steer; three pigeons so that one wrong bird could be outvoted; a nose cone survives at the National Museum of American History

B. F. Skinner, 'Pigeons in a Pelican', American Psychologist 15 (1960): the project got a $25,000 contract in 1943, worked in demonstrations but was not taken up and was cancelled; revived by the Navy as Project ORCON until 1953
